metrics.denominator: eligible observations that have a supplied reference judgment for the pinned release
metrics.note: WP-18 deliberately stores no expected answer, so the denominator counts supplied reference judgments and not cases. With no judgment port wired, this is NO_REFERENCE_JUDGMENT and not a zero.
metrics.numerator: eligible observations whose calculated attention level, coverage status and firing rule identity all equal the reference judgment's
metrics.plain_meaning: Of the eligible cases where a reference judgment says what the answer should be, how many did the system match exactly.
metrics.title: Guideline and rule concordance

metrics.denominator: eligible observations that have a supplied reference judgment for the pinned release
metrics.note: Kept separate from concordance on purpose. Right answer, wrong coverage reason is a real defect that a combined metric hides.
metrics.numerator: eligible observations whose coverage status and coverage reason code equal the reference judgment's
metrics.plain_meaning: Of the eligible cases with a reference judgment, how many had exactly the right coverage status and reason code - independently of whether the attention level matched.
metrics.title: Coverage correctness

metrics.denominator: eligible observations executed under the pinned release
metrics.note: This is NOT WP-20's detector result. WP-20 proved that a detector rejects 36 constructed unsafe states; that says nothing about how a real case behaves under a real release. Reusing that number here would be the exact substitution this work package exists to prevent.
metrics.numerator: eligible observations emitting LOW or NO_ACTIVE_ATTENTION while coverage was not FULL
metrics.plain_meaning: How many eligible cases produced LOW or NO_ACTIVE_ATTENTION when the required inputs were absent - a reader told 'no risk' where the truth is 'we did not look'.
metrics.title: Unsafe false reassurance

metrics.denominator: eligible observations executed under the pinned release
metrics.note: A zero here is only meaningful beside its denominator. Zero over zero is unavailable, and the artifact keeps both numbers so a reader never has to trust the ratio alone.
metrics.plain_meaning: The same finding as a proportion of eligible cases.
metrics.title: Unsafe false reassurance rate

metrics.note: The denominator is findings, not cases. One case can emit several findings and a case-level denominator would let a single untraceable finding hide behind a traceable sibling.
metrics.numerator: emitted findings with at least one resolvable, pinned evidence reference
metrics.plain_meaning: How many emitted findings carried at least one evidence reference that resolves inside the pinned release.
metrics.title: Evidence traceability

metrics.plain_meaning: The same finding as a proportion of emitted findings.
metrics.title: Evidence traceability rate

metrics.denominator: eligible observations executed with at least two declared repeats
metrics.note: Computable over development cases too, because determinism is a software property rather than a scientific claim - so this is reported per role and marked not-validation-evidence. A single repeat cannot show repeatability, so the denominator counts only observations that actually repeated.
metrics.numerator: eligible observations whose output hash was identical across every declared repeat
metrics.plain_meaning: How many eligible cases produced a byte-identical result on every repeat under the same pinned release.
required_inputs: a repeat count of at least two
metrics.title: Deterministic repeatability

metrics.denominator: eligible observations executed with at least two declared repeats
metrics.plain_meaning: The same finding as a proportion of repeated cases.
required_inputs: a repeat count of at least two
metrics.title: Deterministic repeatability rate

metrics.denominator: holdout observations with a supplied reference judgment
metrics.note: Reported separately for INTERNAL_HOLDOUT and EXPERT_HOLDOUT. There is no combined holdout figure: the two partitions answer different questions and pooling them would let a large, easy partition carry a small, hard one.
metrics.numerator: holdout observations satisfying concordance, coverage correctness and evidence traceability together
metrics.plain_meaning: How many holdout cases the system got fully right - attention, coverage and evidence all correct against the reference judgment.
metrics.title: Holdout pass count

metrics.denominator: holdout observations with a supplied reference judgment
metrics.plain_meaning: The same finding as a proportion of judged holdout cases.
metrics.title: Holdout pass rate

metrics.denominator: expert-holdout observations with a completed, post-reveal expert decision
metrics.note: Three counts, never one score. Collapsing agree/partial/disagree into a single percentage would hide whether the disagreements clustered on the dangerous cases.
metrics.plain_meaning: How named expert reviewers judged the system's output on expert-holdout cases: agree, partially agree, or disagree.
metrics.title: Expert agreement distribution

metrics.denominator: expert-holdout observations with a completed rating for that dimension
metrics.note: Optional in the architecture, so its absence is not itself a blocker; it is unavailable like any other unmeasured thing.
metrics.numerator: expert ratings at each Likert point, per dimension
metrics.plain_meaning: Optional expert ratings on declared dimensions such as clarity and clinical usefulness.
metrics.title: Expert Likert dimensions

metrics.denominator: eligible observations executed under the pinned release
metrics.note: A count with no rate on purpose. One unresolved conflict is a finding to act on; expressing it as a small percentage of a large run would make it look like noise.
metrics.numerator: eligible observations reporting a conflict with no applicable precedence rule
metrics.plain_meaning: How many eligible cases ended with two validated sources or rules disagreeing and no declared precedence to settle it.
metrics.title: Unresolved source conflicts

metrics.denominator: the size of the predeclared failure-path catalogue
metrics.note: The denominator is the catalogue, never the set of paths that happened to run. A run touching two paths reports 2/10, not 2/2.
metrics.numerator: distinct failure path ids from the catalogue observed at least once in this run
metrics.plain_meaning: How many of the predeclared failure paths this benchmark actually exercised.
metrics.title: Failure-path coverage

metrics.denominator: the size of the predeclared failure-path catalogue
metrics.plain_meaning: The same finding as a proportion of the catalogue.
metrics.title: Failure-path coverage rate

threshold_policy: No metric carries a threshold. A release threshold is a policy decision made by named people before results exist, with recorded provenance. No such policy exists for this system, so every threshold is null. A threshold added after seeing results would describe those results rather than judge them.

unavailable_reasons.BENCHMARK_NOT_EXECUTED: no benchmark run exists; nobody looked
unavailable_reasons.CASE_MANIFEST_HASH_MISMATCH: the case manifest hash disagrees with the one the plan pinned
unavailable_reasons.INPUT_INCOMPATIBLE: the supplied input does not satisfy this metric's declared requirements
unavailable_reasons.NO_ACTIVE_RELEASE: no release is registered or active, so nothing can be pinned and no benchmark can name what it measured
unavailable_reasons.NO_COMPLETED_EXPERT_REVIEWS: this metric summarises what named experts decided under the blind protocol; the protocol and the review module exist and no expert has completed a review
unavailable_reasons.NO_ELIGIBLE_OBSERVATIONS: no observation in this run belongs to a role this metric may be computed over
unavailable_reasons.NO_HOLDOUT_CASES: no case is held out from development, so nothing here measures generalisation
unavailable_reasons.NO_REFERENCE_JUDGMENT: this metric compares an output against a reference judgment, and no reference judgment has been supplied; WP-18 stores no expected answer, by design
unavailable_reasons.RELEASE_HASH_MISMATCH: an observation names a release or manifest hash that disagrees with the pinned one
unavailable_reasons.RELEASE_NOT_PINNED: the benchmark plan does not pin one release with all required hashes
unavailable_reasons.RESTRICTED_STORAGE_NOT_CONFIGURED: holdout payloads live in restricted storage and none is configured, so the cases could not be executed
unavailable_reasons.SEPARATION_AUDIT_FAILED: the development/holdout separation audit is not clean, so no metric may be computed from this case set at all
unavailable_reasons.ZERO_DENOMINATOR: the denominator this metric divides by is zero, so there is no rate to report; zero and one hundred would both be inventions
